t: That paragraph VIII of Veterans Regulation Numbered 10, as amended by Public Law 439, Seventy-eighth Congress, is hereby further amended by striking out the period and substituting a colon therefor and adding the following: “Provided, however, That disease, injury, or death incurred without willful misconduct on the part of the service person shall be deemed to have been incurred in line of duty if the sentence of the court martial did not involve an unremitted dishonorable discharge or if the offense for which convicted by civil court did not involve a felony as defined under the laws of the jurisdiction where the service person was convicted by such civil court.”

fable.w: This section amends a veterans regulation to define when disease, injury, or death is deemed incurred in line of duty. The references to a court martial and a civil court might tempt a reading that some outside process is involved, but those are past adjudications used only as eligibility criteria, not a consultation, hearing, comment process, or right to sue over a federal decision. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: shall be deemed to have been incurred in line of duty if the sentence of the court martial did not involve an unremitted dishonorable discharge

qwen_block.w: This section amends a regulation to define when a disease, injury, or death is deemed to have been incurred in the line of duty for veterans' benefits purposes. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in a federal decision-making process. It is a substantive definition of eligibility criteria, not a procedural requirement for public input.
qwen_block.s: That paragraph VIII of Veterans Regulation Numbered 10, as amended by Public Law 439, Seventy-eighth Congress, is hereby further amended by striking out the period and substituting a colon therefor and adding the following: “Provided, however, That disease, injury, or death incurred without willful misconduct on the part of the service person shall be deemed to have been incurred in line of duty if the sentence of the court martial did not involve an unremitted dishonorable discharge or if the offense for which convicted by civil court did not involve a felony as defined under the laws of the jurisdiction where the service person was convicted by such civil court.”

opus.w: Congress directly amends the text of an existing veterans regulation to set a substantive line-of-duty rule. It does not authorize any agency to issue regulations, and it does not require consultation, hearings, advisory bodies, or a right to sue. The references to courts-martial and civil courts concern a service member's past convictions, not a challenge to a federal decision. The fact that the section amends a regulation does not make it a grant of rulemaking authority.
opus.s: That paragraph VIII of Veterans Regulation Numbered 10, as amended by Public Law 439, Seventy-eighth Congress, is hereby further amended by striking out the period and substituting a colon therefor and adding the following:
opus.b:
1. **Analysis.** There are two tempting but wrong readings. One is that the section involves rulemaking because it amends "Veterans Regulation Numbered 10." But here Congress itself rewrites the regulation's text. It doesn't give an agency authority to issue regulations, so the rulemaking criterion isn't met. The other is the mention of courts-martial and civil courts. Those refer to a service member's past convictions, used to decide whether an injury counts as "in line of duty." They don't give any outside party a right to sue over a federal decision. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a regulation to define when a service member's injury or death is considered 'in line of duty' for benefits purposes. It establishes eligibility criteria but does not require the government to consult with veterans, the public, or any outside entity before making a decision. There is no mention of public comment, hearings, advisory boards with outside members, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_chat.s: Provided, however, That disease, injury, or death incurred without willful misconduct on the part of the service person shall be deemed to have been incurred in line of duty if the sentence of the court martial did not involve an unremitted dishonorable discharge or if the offense for which convicted by civil court did not involve a felony as defined under the laws of the jurisdiction where the service person was convicted by such civil court.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the amendment affects veterans (outside the government) and thus involves them. However, the text merely defines eligibility criteria for benefits ("deemed to have been incurred in line of duty"). It does not require the government to consult with veterans, hold hearings, or seek their input before making a decision. It is a substantive definition of eligibility, not a procedural requirement for participation.
